mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a New Zealand notary public followed by an Apostille from the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade for any destination state that is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention. For a non-member destination state, use parallel consular legalization at that state's embassy or consulate in New Zealand; apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original certificate notarized by a New Zealand notary public and authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade Apostille. If the receiving jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention member, the notarized certificate must instead be submitted to the destination consulate for consular legalization; the two authentication methods are parallel and never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Board of Directors (post-incorporation board action)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signatures of directors and any attorney-in-fact verified by a New Zealand notary public, then MFAT Apostille for Hague-member destination states; for non-Hague destination states, obtain consular legalization independently from the destination state's consular office. Do not add an apostille to a document to be consularized or vice versa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Initial Shareholders and Directors of the New Zealand Limited Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy of the executed constitution certified by a director or company secretary, notarized by a New Zealand notary, then authenticated by MFAT Apostille for Apostille Convention countries; for non-members, use consular legalization only and never combine the two legalization chains.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Registered Bank maintaining the company's transaction account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank reference letter on bank letterhead issued and authenticated by a bank officer, notarized by a New Zealand notary, then MFAT Apostille for Apostille Convention destination states; for non-member destination states, the notarized letter is submitted directly for consular legalization at the destination state's consulate. Apostille and consular legalization remain parallel and mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct risk-based four-factor screening at formation and continuously thereafter: (1) screen all individuals with 25% or more beneficial ownership or significant control, directors, senior managers, authorized signatories, and persons holding powers of attorney; (2) run automated and manual checks against the New Zealand Police financial intelligence unit PEP databases, Financial Markets Authority disqualification and banning registers, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated List, UK consolidated sanctions list, and all measures issued under the Sanctions Act 2019; (3) retain a five-year audit trail of screening results, source-of-funds, source-of-wealth, and each adverse media hit; (4) escalate any PEP, sanctions, or adverse-media match to the AML/CFT compliance officer and file a suspicious transaction report with the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit where required, with independent third-party verification of identity and nominee disallowance unless fully disclosed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Name Availability Search and Online Registration Portal (companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Companies Act 1993 and Companies Office naming guidelines, a proposed limited company name must be expressed in roman alphabetic or numerical characters; Te Reo Maori and other non-English words may be used but the official register does not recognize macrons or diacritical marks, and any foreign script must be accompanied by a phonetic transliteration or English translation where necessary. The four-tier naming doctrine requires: (1) a distinctive identity element; (2) a descriptive commercial activity element; (3) a mandatory legal-form suffix such as Limited or Ltd; and (4) a restricted-token review for any sensitive or prohibited word before registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 20 working days of a name rejection, file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies, explaining why the proposed name is not false, misleading, offensive, prohibited, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, and attach supporting evidence such as a registered trade mark, prior ministerial consent, or a statutory interpretation. If the Registrar declines the reconsideration, file an application for judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972 within 28 days of the refusal. A reserved name may generally be extended for one further 30-day period online if not yet used, but a rejected name cannot be extended and a fresh application is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The Companies Act 1993 requires every New Zealand company to maintain a registered office in New Zealand at a physical address where documents may be served, and it does not expressly prohibit a service-provider address or virtual office if that address is a real street address. However, for a high-risk peer-to-peer micro-lending fintech under ISIC 6499, the Financial Markets Authority, the Inland Revenue Department, and tier-1 New Zealand banks uniformly reject a bare commercial mailbox or virtual office as sufficient commercial substance for an AML/CFT-licensed platform; they require a physical operational presence, identifiable management, local employment substance, access to books and records, and a genuine place of business in New Zealand.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 15% for a standard low-risk New Zealand company, rising to 40% in the first 12 months for a high-risk P2P micro-lending fintech relying solely on a virtual office. Checklist for unannounced inspections by Inland Revenue, the Financial Markets Authority, or the Companies Office: (a) physical reception with clear company signage; (b) employees or responsible personnel present during normal business hours; (c) statutory registers and board minutes accessible on site; (d) AML/CFT compliance policies and screening records available for review; (e) bank account records and signatory lists matching filed directors; (f) physical filing systems or servers demonstrating substantive operational management in New Zealand.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993, New Zealand, especially Part 2 Incorporation and Part 5 Shares; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 Part 6; Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; Credit Contracts and Consumer Finance Act 2003; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Application for Registration of a Company, filed electronically through the New Zealand Companies Office online register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement; incorporation may proceed with one subscriber share issued at NZ$1. The share issue price, if any, must be recorded in the share register and paid wholly or partly as required by Part 5 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE DIRECTORS OF [NZ LTD] (THE COMPANY) ADOPTED THIS DAY UNDER THE COMPANIES ACT 1993. 1. The directors, constituting a quorum, unanimously resolve that the shareholding structure shown in the incorporation application is ratified and that each subscriber identified in the share register has been allotted the number of ordinary shares set opposite their name. 2. The directors resolve that all shares allotted under the incorporation application are fully or partly paid in accordance with section 37 of the Companies Act 1993, that any outstanding issue price is recorded in the share register, and that consideration other than cash is lawful and evidenced by a written valuation retained in the company records. 3. The directors approve and adopt the registered office at the address filed with the Registrar of Companies, being a physical address in New Zealand, and authorize the secretary to give all notices required by sections 188 and 189 of the Companies Act 1993 in respect of registered office and records address. 4. The directors approve the opening of bank accounts with a licensed New Zealand registered bank and resolve that payments of client funds, if held, be segregated from corporate funds and that the lending platform settle borrower repayments only into a trust account approved by the Financial Markets Authority. 5. The directors resolve that any two directors, or one director jointly with the chief financial officer, are authorized to sign cheques and electronic payment instructions and that all bank mandates comply with the company's anti-money laundering and countering financing of terrorism programme. 6. The directors appoint [NAME] as chair, [NAME] as company secretary, [NAME] as chief financial officer, and [NAME] as AML/CFT compliance officer, each appointment to take effect immediately. 7. The directors authorize management to apply for the peer-to-peer lending licence, financial service provider registration, credit business registration, and all other statutory permissions necessary to carry on micro-lending through the platform. 8. The directors confirm that the statutory registers, minute book, and share register will be kept at the registered office and that this resolution is signed by all directors present and deposited in the minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability and Pre-Incorporation Eligibility Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Online Name Search and Reservation Facility, MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform the pre-incorporation integrity and name availability check against the New Zealand Register of Companies through the Companies Office search and reserve name facility. Reserve the proposed name, if desired, before drafting the incorporation application. Confirm that no reserved or registered company uses the same name or a confusingly similar name, and that words such as bank, trust or insurance are not included unless the applicant holds the specific statutory authorisation. Prepare the company constitution and the subscribers consent, specify the initial shareholding, and confirm that the registered office address in New Zealand is a physical address and not a post office box. Collate certified identity documents and signed consent forms of each founding director.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and optional name reservation receipt
Companies Act Part 2 constitution, signed by subscribers
Consent to appointment as director from each founding director
Registered office physical address and service of process details
Share allocation schedule and subscriber particulars
Certified passports or national identity documents for directors and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office refuses a name or serves an objection, the applicant may submit an alternative name or provide evidence of written consent from the objecting holder within one month. The applicant may also request a name review through the Companies Office query procedure. A name reservation rejection does not forfeit the incorporation fee if the application is not yet filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Form 1 and Commercial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office online portal, RealMe authenticated
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the complete registration application through the Companies Office online portal using a RealMe login and pay the prescribed MBIE filing fee. The system validates that every director has given signed consent, the registered office is in New Zealand, and the proposed capital structure is lawful. Upon successful lodgement, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, a unique company number and a New Zealand Business Number. This step transforms the disclosed structure into a separate legal person with limited liability. The company must thereafter maintain its statutory registers and file the annual return. Any defect in the electronic form will suspend processing and require correction before the certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Completed Form 1 - Application for Registration of a Company
Signed constitution and subscriber consents
Directors consent forms
Share register and initial allotment schedule
Registered office address declaration
Fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects or suspends the application, the online defect notice will specify the non-compliant fields. The applicant should correct and resubmit through the portal or apply for administrative reconsideration. A prompt cure preserves the original lodgement date if the Registrar accepts the correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue, New Zealand, myIR secure online business gateway
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register the company with Inland Revenue so that it receives an income tax number and, where taxable turnover exceeds NZ$60,000 in any twelve-month period, a GST registration number. The company must declare its financial balance date, complete the online business registration, and confirm whether employer registration, PAYE, resident withholding tax and fringe benefit tax apply. For a peer-to-peer lending fintech, platform commissions, loan recovery fees and interest flows must be mapped for GST and income tax treatment. The director or designated tax agent should download the myIR credentials, link the New Zealand Business Number, and note that annual returns to the Companies Office and tax returns to Inland Revenue carry separate statutory deadlines.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number confirmation
Online tax registration form
Director identification documents
Registered office and postal address
Shareholders list with tax file numbers
Bank confirmation of company trading account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue issues a query or a non-registration notice, the applicant should respond through myIR within 15 working days with the Certificate of Incorporation and corrected business details. Where a late registration penalty is proposed, the company may apply to Inland Revenue for remission under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and provide evidence that the failure was not due to gross negligence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitutional Mechanics, Statutory Registers, and Banking Mandate Execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company and the licensed trading bank selected under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a properly constituted meeting of the board or execute the unanimous written resolution, adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, ratify the registered office, and open the company operational bank account. The board appoints the chair, company secretary, chief financial officer and AML/CFT compliance officer and records their signed consents. The bank must perform customer due diligence on all directors and beneficial owners under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. If the platform will handle client money, the board must direct that repayments and lender funds be held in a segregated trust account and that the operating account signs by any two directors or one director with the chief financial officer. Minutes and registers must be kept at the registered office.
required_dossiers: First board resolution and signed minutes
Certificate of Incorporation
Directors certified passports and proof of residential address
Beneficial ownership declaration
AML/CFT awareness training certificates for directors
Bank account application and signatory mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank declines account opening for customer due diligence failure, provide corrected certified identity documents or use the bank reregistration process. If the bank remains unwilling to onboard the entity, the board may appoint another registered bank and execute a new banking mandate; there is no Registrar remedy because banking relationships are commercial contracts governed by mandatory customer due diligence rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial Markets, Consumer Credit and AML/CFT Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Markets Authority and Financial Service Providers Register administered by the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the regulated financial services application before offering peer-to-peer micro-lending to the public. Apply to the Financial Markets Authority for a peer-to-peer lending service market services licence or rely on a valid exemption, and concurrently update the Financial Service Providers Register through the Companies Office. Prepare the informational filing including the governing compliance manual, dispute resolution membership, disclosure statement, credit policies under the Credit Contracts and Consumer Finance Act 2003, loan book controls, and the AML/CFT risk and compliance programme. The responsible person must demonstrate fitness and propriety, and the board must approve the outsourcing arrangements for payment rails including ACH direct debit and local wallet payout. A full licence decision requires the FMA to be satisfied as to the applicant's capability to comply with fair dealing and disclosure obligations.
required_dossiers: FMA peer-to-peer lending licence application and filing fee
Financial Service Providers Register application
Disclosure statement and lending terms
AML/CFT compliance programme and risk assessment
External dispute resolution membership evidence
Fitness and propriety declarations for all directors
Privacy, data protection and cyber security policies
Auditor or governance sign-off on loan underwriting algorithm
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FMA issues a further information notice under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, the applicant must respond within ten working days or within the period stated in the notice. If the application is refused, the company may apply to the High Court for judicial review or submit a revised application after curing corporate governance, capital, or compliance deficiencies. The platform must not accept new lender commitments while the licence or registration is suspended.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - financial technology lending platform; no industrial plant or physical manufacturing site exists. The relevant statutory authorising bodies are the Financial Markets Authority, the Financial Service Providers Register, and the AML/CFT supervisor, not an industrial licensing board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Peer-to-peer lending service market services licence under Part 6 of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; Financial Service Provider registration under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; Credit Business registration under the Credit Contracts and Consumer Finance Act 2003; AML/CFT reporting entity registration under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the Environmental Protection Authority is not engaged because the company has no physical installation, industrial plant, or land-disturbing activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no full EIA, Environmental Registration, or Exemption certificate is required for an algorithm-only lending platform; if the company later occupies a warehouse or server room, local territorial authority resource consent may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the digital platform generates no wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams. Any occupied office must comply with usual municipal building standards; electrical and data equipment disposal must follow the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and producer responsibility requirements if applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defence fire permit, structural load inspection, or industrial workplace safety approval is required for a digital lending platform. The company remains subject to the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 for any leased office, and the building owner must maintain a current warrant of fitness for non-industrial premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue, Te Tari Taake) of New Zealand; official electronic portal is myIR at https://myir.ird.govt.nz. Inland Revenue administers the Income Tax Act 2007, the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, the Tax Administration Act 1994, and related legislation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step-by-step procurement of the New Zealand tax identity for a foreign-owned NZ limited company: (1) Incorporate under the Companies Act 1993 and obtain the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) from the New Zealand Companies Office; the company number and NZBN are not tax identifiers. (2) Apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD Number using form IR596 (Non-resident company IRD number application) or online via myIR, providing the certificate of incorporation, NZ registered office address, director and ultimate beneficial owner particulars, tax residence of each shareholder, and the nature and place of the proposed business activities. (3) If the company will carry on a taxable activity in New Zealand or supply remote services to New Zealand consumers, register for GST (form IR356 or online in myIR) at the same time; the GST registration number is the same as the IRD Number. (4) Obtain a Customs client code from the New Zealand Customs Service for any physical import or export of goods; this code is not required for pure services or financial services. (5) For a regulated financial-services entity, complete the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) application and join an approved dispute-resolution scheme under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 before commencing lending activities; this is a licensing obligation, but Inland Revenue operationally cross-checks FSPR registration when processing GST and income-tax registrations. (6) Appoint a New Zealand tax agent or in-country director if the entity has no local operational presence; a non-resident company that is not carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand may still obtain an IRD Number for New Zealand-source income compliance, including withholding tax on interest. Issuance of the IRD Number is free of charge and is a precondition for claiming double-tax-agreement relief, filing returns, and registering for GST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation with a territorial-source overlay. A company incorporated in New Zealand is a New Zealand tax resident (Income Tax Act 2007 s Y 2) and is taxed at the entity level at the corporate rate of 28% on its worldwide income. There is no automatic pass-through; company losses are quarantined in the entity and cannot be utilised by shareholders unless the company elects look-through status. The company may access the New Zealand dividend imputation regime (subpart OB). For a foreign-owned New Zealand limited company, New Zealand-source income (interest, fees, and lending profits sourced to New Zealand) is taxed on assessment; income sourced outside New Zealand is generally outside the New Zealand tax net for a non-resident company but inside the net for a resident company. As the operating lender platform for New Zealand consumers, all platform income from New Zealand borrowers will be New Zealand-source business income. There is no tax-exempt zone or offshore financial-centre classification available to a commercial micro-lending fintech in New Zealand.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box classification election exists in New Zealand; entity classification is determined by legal form and statute. Available statutory elections relevant to this NZ_LTD include: (1) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, available to a company with five or fewer individual or eligible shareholders; the entity becomes fiscally transparent with income, deductions, and credits flowing through to shareholders, subject to shareholder basis limits for losses; the election is irrevocable for five years except with Commissioner consent. (2) Dividend imputation election, allowing the company to maintain an imputation credit account and attach imputation credits to distributions. (3) GST group election under s 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, allowing commonly controlled companies to register as a single GST group and simplifying returns and internal invoicing. (4) Hybrid and branch mismatch rules (ss FH 1 to FH 14) are mandatory and not elective; no check-the-box or pairing election exists for hybrid entities, but the legislation contains ordering and ratio rules and requires contemporaneous documentation of the offshore mismatch analysis. (5) Controlled-foreign-company elections, including the branch-equivalent election where the NZ_LTD holds offshore lending subsidiaries in grey-list jurisdictions; such elections must be made in writing to Inland Revenue before the relevant return due date.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), a value-added tax levied under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (New Zealand)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in a 12-month period (GST Act 1985 s 51). Both a retrospective test (actual supplies in the preceding 12 months exceeded NZD 60,000) and a prospective test (reasonable expectation of exceeding NZD 60,000 in the next 12 months) trigger compulsory registration. A person making only exempt supplies, such as pure credit interest, is not liable to register and cannot claim input credits; the threshold is assessed only against taxable supplies. For non-resident suppliers of remote services, including online platform services to New Zealand consumers, the same NZD 60,000 threshold applies to supplies to New Zealand consumers; below the threshold registration is voluntary but unavailable where the supplier makes only exempt or non-taxable supplies. A P2P lender must map its revenue streams: interest and credit-facility fees are exempt financial supplies (Schedule 3 of the GST Act), while non-financial administration, software subscription, and default-recovery services may be taxable supplies subject to GST and counted toward the registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand operates no real-time fiscal clearance and no mandatory pre-clearance API or digital stamping for tax invoices. The GST compliance framework is periodic and self-assessed: the registered person accounts for GST on a monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly cycle and files form GST101/GST101A via myIR; payment is due on the filing date. Tax invoices must be issued within 28 days of the time of supply and contain the prescribed particulars, including supplier name, GST/IRD number, recipient details, description, date, consideration, and GST amount; debit and credit notes follow the same regime. E-invoicing is voluntary under the PEPPOL-based E-invoicing NZ framework (operated with support from the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment), and Inland Revenue accepts e-invoices as business records; there is no IRD interception or pre-clearance step. For exports of goods, the mandatory electronic export declaration is lodged through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window (customs.govt.nz), and that customs clearance is not a tax function. GST returns and payments must be filed electronically by registered GST entities.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the GST Act 1985: (a) Goods are zero-rated under s 140 where the supplier exports the goods within 28 days of the time of supply in the ordinary course of business and retains documented evidence of physical export from New Zealand; the supplier must be the exporter of record on the customs declaration. (b) Services are zero-rated under s 11A where supplied to a person who is a non-resident and is outside New Zealand at the time the services are supplied, provided the services are not supplied for use directly in a taxable activity carried on in New Zealand and are not directly connected with New Zealand land or goods. For financial services, including the supply of credit, loan arrangement, and loan administration, s 11A zero-rates exported financial services where the recipient is a non-resident person outside New Zealand and the benefit of the service is obtained offshore; anti-avoidance s 11A(3) denies zero-rating if the arrangement has a purpose of avoiding GST and the services are in substance used by a New Zealand resident. The P2P platform must contractually identify the borrower's residence through a non-resident declaration supported by KYC/AML evidence, confirm that the proceeds are drawn and used offshore, and demonstrate that the loan is booked through its offshore lending channel rather than its New Zealand consumer channel. Exempt financial services supplied to New Zealand residents remain GST-exempt, not zero-rated; unsubstantiated zero-rating of such supplies is reassessed at 15%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic declaration lodged through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window, including exporter client code, tariff classification, valuation, and destination evidence) for goods exports
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (original or electronic transport document evidencing dispatch from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply)

Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-currency receipt statement (bank-generated evidence that the export consideration was received into the entity's New Zealand bank account from the overseas customer, substantiating FX repatriation and source)

Non-Resident Services Declaration (for the lending platform: executed loan agreement, borrower KYC/UBO files, and a declaration or contractual warranty confirming that the borrower is non-resident and uses the funds offshore, in support of the s 11A zero-rating of exported financial services)
GST tax invoice and underlying platform fee schedule (demonstrating the classification of each revenue stream as exempt, zero-rated, or taxable and supporting the GST return position)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue applies strict audit scrutiny to export zero-rating and GST refund claims. The taxpayer must retain all export and non-resident supply records for seven years (Tax Administration Act 1994 s 22); failure to do so exposes the entity to a best-judgement assessment under s 106. If zero-rating is not substantiated, the supply is treated as standard-rated at 15% GST, and the claimed refund of output tax and embedded input credits is clawed back together with use-of-money interest from the due date of each return. Shortfall penalties apply on the resulting tax shortfall: 20% for lack of reasonable care; 40% for gross carelessness; 100% for an abusive tax position; and 150% for evasion or an arrangement with a dominant purpose of defeating the tax. Criminal liability under s 143A exposes the company to a fine not exceeding NZD 250,000 and directors or officers to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years, with conviction implicating both the entity and responsible officers. For financial-services exports, Inland Revenue will test commercial substance, authenticity of non-resident declarations, actual cross-border payment flows, and the ultimate use of loan proceeds; a failed offshore treatment is reassessed at 15% on the full consideration plus penalties and interest, and the entity may also face taxpayer-name disclosure under s 77D and loss of GST registration privileges. New Zealand imposes no statutory exchange-control deadline for FX repatriation; the 180-day figure is the operational evidentiary benchmark, meaning the inward-remittance certificate should be obtained and filed within 180 days of the time of supply to satisfy Inland Revenue's export substantiation practice.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Putea Matua) under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989; the Financial Markets Authority also administers the licence for peer-to-peer lending services under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely convertible. New Zealand maintains no general exchange-control regulations for either current or capital account transactions. Profit remittance is unrestricted, but dividends and interest paid to non-residents are subject to New Zealand non-resident withholding tax at treaty rates unless reduced under a Double Tax Agreement. Capital inflows and outflows, including equity injections, loan principal repayments, and trade payments, are not subject to prior approval unless the transaction triggers the Overseas Investment Act for sensitive New Zealand assets.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion requirement exists for NZD. Export receipts may be retained in any currency. Entities must only maintain adequate records for tax returns and for Statistics New Zealand balance-of-payments reporting, including the official financial account balance and accompanying purpose of payment narrative when the local bank submits a regulatory statistical return.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital electronic-money institutions (EMIs) cannot provide New Zealand settlement accounts without a New Zealand banking licence or avoidance of deposit-taking business. No European or UK EMI passporting applies to New Zealand. A licensed peer-to-peer micro-lending platform must hold client money in an independent, NLG-qualified trust account with a registered New Zealand bank, or maintain segregated operational and escrow accounts with a tier-1 registered bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand law does not mandate physical appearance for directors opening a corporate bank account, but a senior compliance officer or director must complete an identity verification procedure. Most tier-1 banks require at least one video-conference interview for non-resident directors or high-risk business models, and may impose an in-person meeting where ultimate beneficial ownership is complex or where the peer-to-peer lending platform presents a higher ML/FT risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business model flagged as a money-lending fintech with automated underwriting and no physical branch.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) peer-to-peer lending service licence, the Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) AML/CFT risk assessment and compliance programme, the New Zealand Companies Office certificate of incorporation, audited financial statements, and a detailed description of the automated underwriting algorithm, including anti-fraud controls and borrower credit-risk governance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders or directors located in a jurisdiction with higher money-laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certified copies of passports, proof of residential address, corporate registry extracts in English, banking references from the home country, and evidence of source of funds for the initial capital injection. If any shareholder holds more than 25% of the company, an Overseas Investment Office clearance or legal opinion confirming no clearance is required must also be provided.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious transaction pattern involving rapid inbound capital injection followed by immediate disbursement to external borrowers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce a board-approved funds-flow policy, a customer due diligence procedure, a transaction-monitoring system report, a sanctions screening certificate, and an independent AML/CFT audit prepared in accordance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. A complete funding register showing the source and final use of each borrower loan may also be required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions must be wired via SWIFT MT103 with a detailed payment description specifying 'Equity injection for operational working capital under the BPM6 financial account'. The sending bank should include the final beneficiary: NZ_LTD, with the registered office address and New Zealand bank account number. The local receiving bank may require a company resolution authorising the capital injection and the statutory declaration of origin of funds for AML purposes. For share capital exceeding certain thresholds, the register of overseas investment must be checked, and any applicable exemption certificate should be retained by the treasurer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic borrower disbursements should use the New Zealand Bulk Electronic Clearing System (BECS) direct debit and the local wallet payout rails for micro consumer loans, executed on a daily netting cycle. Cross-border payments, including any platform suppliers or lenders, should use SWIFT MT103 with standard settlement instructions. Trade settlements involving letters of credit must be routed through a confirming New Zealand bank using commercial documentary credits, with all bill of lading and invoice documentation matched to the ISIC 6499 lending portfolio.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts on NZD/USD and NZD/EUR with licensed New Zealand banks
Cross-currency swaps for matching long-term foreign-currency funding to NZD lending assets
Option-based currency hedging strategies including vanilla FX options where the underlying is a confirmed cross-border receivable or payable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Registrar of Companies (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due during the anniversary month of incorporation; filing must be completed by the last day of the month in which the incorporation anniversary falls
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of NZ$50 applies after the anniversary month; repeated non-filing for two consecutive years triggers s 318 removal notices and can result in administrative strike-off of the company from the New Zealand Companies Register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and Annual Report (Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Registrar of Companies; Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for licensed peer-to-peer lending service providers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be filed with the Registrar within 5 months after balance date; FMC reporting entities must send the annual report to shareholders within 4 months after balance date and file it with the FMA and the Registrar at the same time
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Continuing default exposes the company and every director to monetary penalties under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and the FMC Act; the Registrar may issue compliance notices, and the FMA may take licensing and enforcement action under the FMC Act, including financial penalties and suspension of the P2P lending licence

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent AML/CFT Programme Audit (Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, s 59)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) as the AML/CFT sector supervisor for licensed peer-to-peer lending services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once in every 2-year period; the audit report must be completed, retained for review, and produced to the FMA upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Breach of s 59 is a civil liability act under the AML/CFT Act; the FMA may impose pecuniary penalties, civil remedies, compliance orders, or escalate to FMC Act licensing sanctions against the P2P lending platform

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is compulsory for FMC reporting entities (including all licensed peer-to-peer lending services) regardless of size under the FMC Act 2013. For non-FMC companies, the Companies Act 1993 audit exemption applies unless the company is 'large' (exceeding at least two of three thresholds for two consecutive accounting periods: NZ$5.5 million total assets; NZ$11 million total revenue; 25 employees) or shareholders holding 5% or more of voting rights request an audit (s 199 Companies Act 1993).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand IFRS (Tier 1 full IFRS as adopted by the External Reporting Board) for FMC reporting entities; Tier 2 NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR) applies only where the entity is not publicly accountable; financial statements must comply with the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand law does not require a separate annual UBO filing; the Companies Register is updated continuously for share allotments and transfers (notice to the Registrar within 20 working days), and shareholder ownership details are reconfirmed in each Annual Return. As an AML/CFT reporting entity, the platform must verify beneficial owners at onboarding and refresh beneficial ownership information on a risk-sensitive basis, with enhanced due diligence review at least annually for high-risk customers; the independent AML/CFT programme audit (at least every 2 years) verifies the adequacy and currency of beneficial ownership controls and records.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120-350 per annum (NZ$200-550) for a registered office and registered agent in New Zealand; a full corporate secretarial and annual return administration package typically ranges from USD 400-900 per annum.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800-9,000 per annum (NZ$3,000-15,000) for a certified audit of a micro-lending fintech under NZ IFRS; an additional USD 800-2,500 per annum is typical for the separate AML/CFT programme audit where not bundled.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays for P2P micro-lending conduct. The substantial R&D Tax Credit regime (15% of eligible R&D expenditure) may apply to platform software/algorithm development. Imputation credits may effectively lower the combined corporate and shareholder tax burden for New Zealand-resident shareholders.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (subject to shareholder continuity of at least 49%, or the same or similar business continuity test)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically via Inland Revenue's myIR portal or approved e-filing software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (income year), with provisional tax instalments for larger taxpayers typically due on 7 August, 15 January, and 7 May
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be filed by 7 July after the income year end (or by 7 April for taxpayers not using a tax agent, subject to Inland Revenue extension policies). Non-standard balance dates have corresponding month-7 deadlines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income from all taxable business activities, including gross interest, fee income, platform administration charges, and any incidental revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident company without a New Zealand permanent establishment (PE), report only New Zealand-sourced income attributable to lending activities or platform users. If no NZ-source income and no PE, an IR4 is generally not required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total allowable deductions, including direct operating costs, credit underwriting automation expenses, bad debts (tax-allowable), interest on borrowed funds, and platform maintenance costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be allocated to New Zealand business income. Non-residents are subject to transfer pricing rules and thin capitalisation restrictions (NZ$10 million threshold), so intercompany funding costs must be arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or net loss after deducting Box 6B from Box 6A. A loss here may be carried forward under continuity rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident company with a PE, report only the profit attributable to that PE under Article 7 of the applicable DTA; use of internal funding must be supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after offset of carried-forward losses. This is the amount subject to income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may not use NZ tax losses unless they arise from an NZ PE and continuity requirements are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on taxable income calculated at the 28% corporate rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute at 28%; no graduated corporate rates apply. The PE's taxable income is taxed at this flat rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: resident withholding tax (RWT) on interest income, provisional tax paid, imputation credits, and other allowable credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies may only claim RWT credits withheld on NZ-sourced interest; imputation credits are generally not refundable to non-residents. Foreign tax credits available under DTA articles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual tax payable or refundable. This is the net tax position after subtracting Box 9 from Box 8.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any terminal tax must be paid by the terminal tax date (generally 7 April for 31 March balance dates). Late payment triggers use-of-money interest and penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of IR4 attracts a late filing penalty under section 139A of the Tax Administration Act 1994: NZ$250 for the first month, with additional penalties for continued default (capped at NZ$500 for private service returns in certain cases), plus an automatic late payment penalty of 1% of the unpaid tax on day 1 and 4% from day 8. Use-of-money interest accrues daily on unpaid terminal tax at the prescribed rate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends: 15% on fully imputed dividends; 30% on unimputed dividends. Treaty rates may reduce this to 0-15% depending on ownership and jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double tax agreement (DTA) reduction or exemption on dividends, interest, or royalties, the non-resident recipient must obtain an official Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority, complete Inland Revenue's NRWT reduction declaration (form IR67), and deliver this to the New Zealand payer before or at the time of payment. The payer then withholds at the treaty rate; if the certificate is received after payment, a tax refund must be claimed through Inland Revenue. In all cases, the beneficiary must be the beneficial owner, not a conduit or shell, and must have economic substance in their state of residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: NRWT statutory 15%; most NZ DTAs provide a 10% or 5% treaty rate for industrial or copyright royalties, provided TRC and beneficial ownership documentation are in place. Interest: NRWT statutory 15%; an alternative Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may apply on interest paid to an approved non-resident lender (not associated with the borrower), replacing NRWT entirely. AIL does not apply to dividends. Non-arm's length intercompany interest may be adjusted under transfer pricing rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: required where the New Zealand taxpayer's cross-border related-party transactions (including interest on related-party debt, management fees, software licensing, and lending platform royalty payments) exceed NZ$10 million in aggregate for an income year. Master File: required for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue exceeding NZ$1.3 billion (approximately €750 million). Country-by-Country reporting applies at the same global revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code. However, economic substance is mandated indirectly by the Income Tax Act 2007: section BG 1 general anti-avoidance rule, transfer pricing rules in sections GC 1-GC 15, and the 'business continuity' test for loss utilisation. Non-resident lenders and platform operators must demonstrate real management, decision-making, and risk-taking in New Zealand to avoid a sham or GAAR assessment and to access treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting gross interest or fee income from the IR4, falsifying loan loss deductions, or using undisclosed related-party accounts to shelter P2P lending profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under sections 143A and 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994; on conviction, a fine of up to NZ$250,000 for a company, plus a 150% shortfall penalty under section 141E for evasion or fraudulent intent. Interest on unpaid tax accrues from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in filing false returns are personally liable for penalties and may be imprisoned for up to 5 years. The corporate veil is pierced for fraudulent or sham conduct, exposing directors' personal assets and subjecting them to travel bans and forced civil restitution in civil recovery proceedings by the Commissioner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring related-party lending by charging above-market interest or fees to shift profits to a low-tax jurisdiction, or allocating equity risk to a tax haven while the actual treasury function is performed in New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustments under sections GC 1-GC 15, with taxable income recomputed at arm's length. Shortfall penalties range from 20% (failure to take reasonable care) to 150% (evasion); use-of-money interest applies. A minimum 10% penalty may apply for an unacceptable tax position without reasonable grounds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve non-arm's-length intercompany transactions without adequate transfer pricing documentation are personally liable for resulting shortfall penalties if they caused or allowed the company to take an unacceptable tax position. In serious cases, criminal liability for evasion may attach.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating a New Zealand entity as a pure conduit that has no physical office, no local management, no employees, and no substantive underwriting or lending operations, with the sole purpose of claiming New Zealand tax treaty benefits or low-tax status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under the relevant DTA's limitation-of-benefits or beneficial-ownership clauses; application of the general anti-avoidance rule in section BG 1. The entity may be wound up under the Companies Act 1993 if it is a sham or used to defeat creditors. Penalties include 150% shortfall penalties, refusal of refunds, and cancellation of the New Zealand Financial Service Provider licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the entity's unpaid taxes and penalties if the entity is a sham or façade, as the Courts will pierce the corporate veil. Directors can be subject to disqualification from managing companies, travel bans during investigation, and civil recovery of diverted funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an algorithmic P2P micro-lending platform without a compliant anti-money laundering and countering financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) programme, failing to conduct customer due diligence, neglecting suspicious transaction reporting, or issuing consumer loans without the required credit-contract compliance under the Credit Contracts and Consumer Finance Act 2003 (CCCFA).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, civil penalties for a company of up to NZ$2 million for each contravention; the Financial Markets Authority may revoke the financial service provider licence. CCCFA contraventions attract a maximum civil penalty of NZ$600,000 for a company, plus statutory damages to borrowers and loan write-off orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers are personally liable for corporate AML/CFT failures if they consent or are wilfully blind; on conviction, imprisonment of up to 2 years and fines of up to NZ$300,000 per individual. Directors may also be subject to compensation orders and travel bans pending trial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties to non-resident related parties without deducting NRWT or paying the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL), particularly when the non-resident is a related entity in a zero-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer is personally liable for the full amount of NRWT not deducted, plus an absolute-liability shortfall penalty of up to 150% under section 141D of the Tax Administration Act, late-payment penalties, and use-of-money interest. In addition, the transaction may be recharacterised as a dividend subject to further NRWT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid NRWT where the company fails to pay and a director knew of the non-payment and did not have the company go into liquidation or administration (section 149A TAA). Travel bans may be imposed for substantial tax debt (over NZ$10,000) while the director is outside New Zealand.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Misuse of Imputation Credits / Dividend Manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating artificial imputation credits through aggressive tax arbitrage, paying dividends to a non-resident parent in excess of available credits, or misreporting the imputation credit account to reduce NRWT liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imputation penalty tax of 10% of the company's debit balance at balance date, and a credit segregation and late filing penalties under sections 218-219 of the Income Tax Act 2007. The imputation credit account may be cancelled and NRWT recomputed at the 30% unimputed dividend rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false ICA reconciliation statements are personally liable for penalties; in liquidations, the Commissioner may recover from directors for fraudulent preferential payments through imputation debits.
